1.headline: A big fight over Poland's top court
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

There is a big fight in Poland. It is about the top court in the country. On Friday, a judge stopped the head of the court from working. She is the judge with the most years on the court. Now she leads the court.
Poland's president is angry. He says this breaks public order. He was flying to Africa. But he turned back and came home. Hundreds of people also gathered outside the court.
The prime minister leads the government. He says he wants to fix the courts. The two leaders have fought about judges for a long time.
Again, there is a big fight in Poland about its top court. Thank you for listening.

폴란드에서 큰 싸움이 벌어지고 있습니다. 나라의 최고 법원을 둘러싼 싸움입니다. 금요일에 한 판사가 법원장의 업무를 멈추게 했습니다. 그녀는 이 법원에서 가장 오래 일한 판사입니다. 이제 그녀가 법원을 이끕니다.

2.headline: Poland's leaders fight over the top court
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

There is a big political fight in Poland. It is about the country's highest court, the Constitutional Tribunal. This court checks if laws follow the constitution. On Friday, the court made a surprise announcement. Its longest-serving judge stopped the court's president from doing his job. She is now in charge of the court.

Poland's president, Karol Nawrocki, was very unhappy. He said the move was a breach of public order. A breach means breaking a rule. He was flying to Senegal in Africa, but he turned back. According to news reports, hundreds of people gathered outside the court.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk leads the government. He says he wants to restore the rule of law. This means that everyone must follow the same laws. The European Union said the last government hurt the courts.
Why is this important? The court has hardly worked for a long time. The president and the government do not accept each other's judges. This new step may make the fight even bigger.
To sum up, Poland's leaders are fighting over control of the top court. Thank you for listening.

3.headline: Poland's top court in crisis as its head is suspended
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today we start in Poland, where a fight over the country's top court has suddenly grown bigger. Late on Friday, Poland's Constitutional Tribunal made a surprise announcement. The Constitutional Tribunal is the court that decides if laws follow the constitution. It said its longest-serving judge had suspended the court's president, Bogdan Swieczkowski. To suspend someone means to stop them from doing their job for a while. The judge, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, is now in charge of the court.

Poland's president, Karol Nawrocki, reacted strongly. He called the move a breach of public order, which means a serious threat to the normal running of the country. He was on a plane to Senegal, but he cut the trip short and flew back home. According to news reports, hundreds of people gathered outside the court. Some right-wing politicians accused the government of a coup against the court.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk sees things very differently. He says his government is trying to restore the rule of law. The rule of law means that everyone, including leaders, must follow the same laws. The European Union has said that the previous government, led by the Law and Justice party, damaged the courts. Swieczkowski was appointed during that government.

Why does this matter? For years, the government and the president have refused to accept each other's choices of judges. Because of this, the court has been almost unable to work. The new step could make the conflict even deeper.
To sum up, a judge has suspended the head of Poland's top court, and the country's leaders are in an open fight over it. Thank you for listening.

카롤 나브로츠키 폴란드 대통령은 강하게 반발했습니다. 그는 이 조치를 공공질서 위반이라고 불렀는데, 이는 나라의 정상적인 운영에 대한 심각한 위협이라는 뜻입니다. 그는 세네갈로 가는 비행기에 타고 있었지만 일정을 줄이고 귀국했습니다. 보도에 따르면 수백 명의 사람들이 재판소 밖에 모였습니다. 일부 우파 정치인들은 정부가 재판소를 상대로 쿠데타를 벌였다고 비난했습니다.

요약하면, 한 재판관이 폴란드 최고 법원의 수장을 직무 정지시켰고, 나라의 지도자들이 이를 두고 공개적으로 싸우고 있습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Poland's constitutional court chief suspended, sparking political clash
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

We begin in Poland, where a long-running battle over the country's highest court took a dramatic turn late on Friday. The Constitutional Tribunal announced that its longest-serving judge, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, had suspended the tribunal's president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, and taken charge of the court herself.

The reaction was swift. President Karol Nawrocki described the move as a breach of public order. He was on his way to Senegal at the time, but cut the trip short, saying on social media that the president must be in Poland at a moment like this. According to news reports, hundreds of people rallied outside the tribunal under a heavy police presence, and right-wing politicians accused the government of staging a coup against the court.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk rejects that view. He says his government is working to restore the rule of law, which the European Union says was undermined by the previous Law and Justice government. Swieczkowski was appointed under that government, and critics have long argued that the tribunal, reshaped during that period, no longer meets basic standards of independence.

The dispute has effectively paralyzed the tribunal. President Nawrocki has refused to swear in several judges nominated by parliament, while Swieczkowski declined to seat judges elected by the current majority. In short, each side refuses to recognize the other's appointees.

The stakes go well beyond the courtroom. Poland is one of the largest members of the European Union, and the way it runs its courts is closely watched across the bloc. The latest move could deepen the standoff between the president and the government.
To sum up, a senior judge has suspended the head of Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, sparking protests and a sharp clash between the president and the prime minister. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

5.headline: Poland's court crisis boils over as tribunal chief is suspended
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Poland's simmering constitutional crisis boiled over late on Friday, when the Constitutional Tribunal announced that its longest-serving judge, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, had suspended the court's president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, and assumed control of the institution herself.

The move drew an immediate and furious response from President Karol Nawrocki, who branded it a breach of public order. Nawrocki, who had been en route to Senegal, abruptly cut short his trip, declaring on social media that at a moment like this the president must be in Poland. According to news reports, hundreds of demonstrators converged on the tribunal amid a heavy police presence, where right-wing politicians accused the government of orchestrating what they called a coup against the court.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk, for his part, frames the confrontation as part of a broader effort to restore the rule of law, which the European Union maintains was eroded under the previous Law and Justice government. Swieczkowski was installed during that era, and critics have long contended that the tribunal, reshaped after a contentious round of appointments in 2015, no longer meets basic standards of independence and impartiality. Tusk's coalition swept to power in 2023 vowing to undo those changes.

What has emerged is a bitter institutional tug-of-war. Nawrocki, a nationalist elected in 2025, has refused to swear in several judges nominated by parliament, while Swieczkowski declined to seat those chosen by the current majority. With neither camp recognizing the other's appointees, the tribunal has been all but paralyzed. Even the governing coalition has drawn criticism, after parliament last month appointed a close Tusk ally to the bench, a step detractors said sat uneasily with its pledge to restore checks and balances.

The implications extend well beyond Warsaw. Poland is among the European Union's most influential members, and a prolonged standoff over its highest court could leave key legal questions in limbo and strain its relations with Brussels, which has long pressed Warsaw to shore up judicial independence.

To sum up, the suspension of the tribunal's president has thrown Poland's long-running fight over its judiciary into open confrontation, pitting the president squarely against the government. Thank you for listening.

요약하면, 재판소장의 직무 정지로 폴란드 사법부를 둘러싼 오랜 싸움이 공개적인 대립으로 번졌고, 대통령과 정부가 정면으로 맞서게 되었습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

1.headline: People leave a town held by Russia
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
There is news from the war in Ukraine. Russia holds a small town called Oleshky. Life there is very hard. People have little food and medicine.
Russia and Ukraine agreed to stop fighting there for a few days. On Friday, many people left the town by bus. On Saturday, planes took them to Belarus. Then they went on to Ukraine.
The United States helped make this deal. Melania Trump, the wife of the American president, helped too. Ukraine's president said thank you.
This kind of stop in the war is very rare. But the war is not over. The stop was only for a few days.
Again, people from a town held by Russia went back to Ukraine. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
우크라이나 전쟁 소식입니다. 러시아가 올레시키라는 작은 마을을 차지하고 있습니다. 그곳의 생활은 매우 힘듭니다. 사람들에게 음식과 약이 거의 없습니다.
러시아와 우크라이나는 그곳에서 며칠 동안 싸움을 멈추기로 합의했습니다. 금요일에 많은 사람들이 버스를 타고 마을을 떠났습니다. 토요일에는 비행기가 그들을 벨라루스로 데려갔습니다. 그 뒤 그들은 우크라이나로 계속 이동했습니다.
미국이 이 합의를 도왔습니다. 미국 대통령의 부인인 멜라니아 트럼프도 도왔습니다. 우크라이나 대통령은 고맙다고 말했습니다.
전쟁 중에 이런 식으로 싸움을 멈추는 일은 매우 드뭅니다. 하지만 전쟁은 끝나지 않았습니다. 싸움을 멈춘 것은 며칠 동안뿐이었습니다.
다시 말씀드리면, 러시아가 차지한 마을의 사람들이 우크라이나로 돌아갔습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: A short ceasefire helps people leave Oleshky
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today's news is about the war in Ukraine. Russian forces hold a small town called Oleshky in southern Ukraine. Life there has been very hard. Fighting and drones blocked the roads, so there was not enough food or medicine.

Russia and Ukraine agreed to a short ceasefire in the area. A ceasefire means both sides stop fighting for a while. On Friday, buses took people out of the town. On Saturday, four planes flew them to Belarus. From there, they went on to Ukraine. People could also choose to stay or go to Russian areas.
The White House said Melania Trump, the American first lady, helped make the deal. Ukraine's president thanked the United States and Melania Trump.
Why is this important? According to news reports, this is the first pause of its kind in the war. It gave hungry people a way out. But it is small, and it was planned to end on Sunday evening.
To sum up, people from a hungry town held by Russia were able to reach Ukraine during a short ceasefire. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
오늘의 뉴스는 우크라이나 전쟁에 관한 것입니다. 러시아군이 우크라이나 남부의 올레시키라는 작은 마을을 장악하고 있습니다. 그곳의 생활은 매우 힘들었습니다. 전투와 드론이 길을 막아서 음식과 약이 부족했습니다.
러시아와 우크라이나는 이 지역에서 짧은 휴전에 합의했습니다. 휴전이란 양측이 잠시 싸움을 멈추는 것을 뜻합니다. 금요일에 버스가 사람들을 마을 밖으로 데려갔습니다. 토요일에는 비행기 네 대가 그들을 벨라루스로 실어 날랐습니다. 그곳에서 그들은 우크라이나로 계속 이동했습니다. 사람들은 마을에 남거나 러시아 지역으로 가는 것을 선택할 수도 있었습니다.
백악관은 미국의 영부인 멜라니아 트럼프가 이 합의를 도왔다고 밝혔습니다. 우크라이나 대통령은 미국과 멜라니아 트럼프에게 감사를 표했습니다.
이것이 왜 중요할까요? 보도에 따르면 이번 전쟁에서 이런 종류의 중단은 처음입니다. 굶주린 사람들에게 빠져나갈 길이 생겼습니다. 하지만 규모가 작고, 일요일 저녁에 끝날 예정이었습니다.
요약하면, 러시아가 장악한 굶주린 마을의 사람들이 짧은 휴전 기간에 우크라이나에 도착할 수 있었습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Rare local ceasefire lets Oleshky residents reach Ukraine
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today's top story comes from the war in Ukraine. On Saturday, people from a small town held by Russia made their way back to Ukrainian-controlled land. The town is called Oleshky, and it is in the southern Kherson region. Russian forces have controlled it since 2022. The trip was possible because of a rare local ceasefire. A ceasefire means both sides agree to stop fighting for a while.

According to news reports, the residents left the town by bus on Friday. Then four planes carried them to Gomel, a city in Belarus. Red Cross volunteers and medical teams met them there. From Belarus, they continued to Ukraine. People could also choose to go to Russian-held areas or stay at home.

Life in Oleshky has been very hard. Fighting and drones cut the roads that bring in supplies. As a result, there was little food or medicine. About two thousand people were thought to live there. The White House said First Lady Melania Trump helped arrange the deal. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked the United States and Melania Trump.

Why does this matter? Reports describe this as the first humanitarian truce of its kind in the war. A humanitarian truce is a short pause in fighting to help people who are suffering. However, it is small and short. It was set to end on Sunday evening, and the wider war goes on.
To sum up, hundreds of people left a town short of food in occupied Ukraine during a rare, short ceasefire. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.

오늘의 주요 뉴스는 우크라이나 전쟁 소식입니다. 토요일에 러시아가 장악한 작은 마을의 주민들이 우크라이나가 통제하는 지역으로 돌아왔습니다. 이 마을의 이름은 올레시키이며, 남부 헤르손 지역에 있습니다. 러시아군은 2022년부터 이곳을 장악해 왔습니다. 이번 이동은 드물게 성사된 국지적 휴전 덕분에 가능했습니다. 휴전이란 양측이 잠시 싸움을 멈추기로 합의하는 것을 뜻합니다.
보도에 따르면 주민들은 금요일에 버스를 타고 마을을 떠났습니다. 그 뒤 비행기 네 대가 그들을 벨라루스의 도시 호멜로 실어 날랐습니다. 그곳에서 적십자 자원봉사자들과 의료진이 그들을 맞이했습니다. 그들은 벨라루스에서 우크라이나로 계속 이동했습니다. 주민들은 러시아가 장악한 지역으로 가거나 집에 남는 것을 선택할 수도 있었습니다.
올레시키의 생활은 매우 힘들었습니다. 전투와 드론 때문에 물자가 들어오는 길이 끊겼습니다. 그 결과 음식과 약이 거의 없었습니다. 그곳에는 약 2천 명이 사는 것으로 추정되었습니다. 백악관은 멜라니아 트럼프 영부인이 이번 합의를 성사시키는 데 도움을 주었다고 밝혔습니다. 볼로디미르 젤렌스키 우크라이나 대통령은 미국과 멜라니아 트럼프에게 감사를 표했습니다.
이것이 왜 중요할까요? 보도들은 이번 일을 이 전쟁에서 처음 있는 인도적 휴전이라고 설명합니다. 인도적 휴전이란 고통받는 사람들을 돕기 위한 짧은 전투 중단입니다. 하지만 이번 휴전은 규모가 작고 기간도 짧습니다. 일요일 저녁에 끝날 예정이었고, 더 큰 전쟁은 계속되고 있습니다.
요약하면, 드물게 성사된 짧은 휴전 기간에 점령된 우크라이나 지역에서 음식이 부족한 마을의 주민 수백 명이 마을을 떠났습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Oleshky residents reach Ukraine under rare local truce
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Hundreds of residents of a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine have reached Ukrainian-controlled territory, thanks to a rare local ceasefire that has been described as the first humanitarian truce of its kind in the war.

The town, Oleshky, lies in the Kherson region and has been under Russian control since the early weeks of the full-scale invasion in 2022. According to news reports, fighting and drone attacks have cut off supply routes, leaving residents short of food and medicine. Around two thousand people were believed to be living there.

Bus convoys left the town on Friday, when the truce took effect. Melania Trump said the convoy, made up of twenty-five buses, fifty medical workers and ambulances, was ready to evacuate more than seven hundred and fifty people who chose to leave. On Saturday, four planes carrying evacuees landed in Gomel, in southeastern Belarus, where Red Cross volunteers and medical teams were waiting. From there, the group continued to Ukrainian territory. Residents were also given the option of moving to Russian-held areas or staying in the town, which received fresh food and medical supplies. Russia's human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova, said some buses also carried residents who wished to move to Russia.

The White House says First Lady Melania Trump helped broker the deal, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked the United States and Melania Trump for their mediation. Pope Leo the Fourteenth had also urged both sides to allow aid and evacuations.

The truce, however, was limited in time and scope and was due to expire on Sunday evening. Elsewhere, the fighting continued, and Zelenskyy said Russian strikes had left hundreds of thousands of households without power.
To sum up, a short, local ceasefire allowed hundreds of exhausted civilians to leave occupied Oleshky, a rare moment of cooperation in a war that shows no sign of ending. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
우크라이나 남부의 러시아 점령 마을 주민 수백 명이 우크라이나 통제 지역에 도착했습니다. 이번 전쟁에서 처음 있는 인도적 휴전으로 불리는, 드물게 성사된 국지적 휴전 덕분입니다.
올레시키라는 이 마을은 헤르손 지역에 있으며, 2022년 전면 침공 초기 몇 주 만에 러시아의 통제 아래 들어갔습니다. 보도에 따르면 전투와 드론 공격으로 보급로가 끊기면서 주민들은 음식과 약이 부족한 상태였습니다. 그곳에는 약 2천 명이 살고 있는 것으로 추정되었습니다.

휴전이 발효된 금요일에 버스 행렬이 마을을 떠났습니다. 멜라니아 트럼프는 버스 25대와 의료진 50명, 구급차로 이루어진 행렬이 떠나기로 선택한 750명 이상을 대피시킬 준비가 되어 있다고 말했습니다. 토요일에는 피란민을 태운 비행기 네 대가 벨라루스 남동부의 호멜에 착륙했고, 그곳에서 적십자 자원봉사자들과 의료진이 기다리고 있었습니다. 일행은 그곳에서 우크라이나 영토로 계속 이동했습니다. 주민들에게는 러시아가 장악한 지역으로 옮기거나 마을에 남는 선택지도 주어졌고, 마을에는 새 식량과 의료 물자가 들어갔습니다. 러시아의 인권 담당관 야나 란트라토바는 일부 버스가 러시아로 이주하기를 원하는 주민들도 태웠다고 말했습니다.
백악관은 멜라니아 트럼프 영부인이 이번 합의를 중재하는 데 도움을 주었다고 밝혔고, 볼로디미르 젤렌스키 우크라이나 대통령은 미국과 멜라니아 트럼프의 중재에 감사를 표했습니다. 레오 14세 교황도 양측에 구호품 전달과 대피를 허용하라고 촉구한 바 있습니다.
하지만 이번 휴전은 기간과 범위가 제한되어 있었고, 일요일 저녁에 끝날 예정이었습니다. 다른 지역에서는 전투가 계속되었으며, 젤렌스키 대통령은 러시아의 공격으로 수십만 가구가 전기를 쓰지 못하게 되었다고 말했습니다.
요약하면, 짧은 국지적 휴전 덕분에 지친 민간인 수백 명이 점령된 올레시키를 떠날 수 있었습니다. 끝날 기미가 보이지 않는 전쟁 속에서 드문 협력의 순간이었습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

5.headline: Localized truce opens rare escape route from occupied Oleshky
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

In a rare glimmer of cooperation amid a grinding war, hundreds of civilians from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine have made their way back to Ukrainian-controlled territory, under what has been described as the first humanitarian truce of its kind since the full-scale invasion began.

Oleshky, which sits in the Kherson region, fell under Russian control in the opening weeks of the invasion in 2022. Since then, according to news reports, relentless fighting and drone strikes have severed supply routes, leaving its estimated two thousand residents starved of food and medicine and, by many accounts, utterly exhausted.

The evacuation unfolded in stages. Bus convoys pulled out of the town on Friday, as the localized ceasefire took hold. Melania Trump said the convoy, comprising twenty-five buses, fifty medical professionals and a fleet of ambulances, stood ready to carry more than seven hundred and fifty people who voluntarily chose to leave. On Saturday, four aircraft touched down in Gomel, in southeastern Belarus, where Red Cross volunteers and medical teams were on hand to receive the evacuees before they pressed on to Ukrainian soil. Residents were offered a choice: relocate to Ukrainian-held territory, move to areas under Russian control, or remain in the town, which was resupplied with food and medical aid. Russia's ombudswoman, Yana Lantratova, said some buses also carried residents who opted to resettle in Russia.

The White House credits First Lady Melania Trump with helping to broker the arrangement, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly thanked both her and the United States for their mediation. Pope Leo the Fourteenth had likewise pressed both sides to permit aid deliveries and evacuations.

Still, the truce was narrow by design, confined to a single area and set to lapse on Sunday evening. Its modest scope underscores how elusive a broader settlement remains. Even as the convoys moved, Russian strikes elsewhere knocked out electricity to hundreds of thousands of households, Zelenskyy said.

To sum up, a tightly limited ceasefire has allowed hundreds of weary civilians to escape occupied Oleshky, a small but symbolic humanitarian breakthrough in a conflict that remains far from resolved. Thank you for listening.

그럼에도 이번 휴전은 처음부터 범위가 좁게 설계되어 한 지역에만 적용되었고, 일요일 저녁에 끝날 예정이었습니다. 이처럼 제한된 범위는 더 폭넓은 해결이 얼마나 어려운지를 보여 줍니다. 젤렌스키 대통령은 피란 행렬이 이동하는 동안에도 다른 지역에서는 러시아의 공격으로 수십만 가구의 전기가 끊겼다고 말했습니다.
요약하면, 엄격히 제한된 휴전 덕분에 지친 민간인 수백 명이 점령된 올레시키를 벗어날 수 있었습니다. 해결과는 아직 거리가 먼 전쟁 속에서 작지만 상징적인 인도적 돌파구입니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

1.headline: Game company says sorry for Itaewon video
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
A game company said sorry to Korean families. The company makes the game Call of Duty.

The new game is about a war in Korea. The war is not real. But the game used a few seconds of real news video. The video was from the Itaewon disaster in Seoul. In 2022, a huge crowd filled a small street during Halloween. In total, 159 people died.
The families of the victims were very sad and angry. They asked the company to take the video out.
Now the company says sorry. It will remove the video in an update on November 12.
Again, the game company said sorry and will take out the Itaewon video. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
한 게임 회사가 한국의 가족들에게 사과했습니다. 이 회사는 '콜 오브 듀티'라는 게임을 만듭니다.
새 게임은 한국에서 일어나는 전쟁에 관한 이야기입니다. 이 전쟁은 실제가 아닙니다. 하지만 게임에 몇 초 동안 실제 뉴스 영상이 쓰였습니다. 그 영상은 서울 이태원 참사 때의 것이었습니다. 2022년 핼러윈 때 엄청난 인파가 좁은 골목을 가득 메웠습니다. 모두 159명이 목숨을 잃었습니다.
희생자 가족들은 매우 슬퍼하고 화를 냈습니다. 그들은 회사에 그 영상을 빼 달라고 요청했습니다.
이제 회사는 사과한다고 말합니다. 회사는 11월 12일 업데이트에서 그 영상을 삭제할 예정입니다.
다시 말씀드리면, 게임 회사가 사과했고 이태원 영상을 빼기로 했습니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Call of Duty maker apologizes for Itaewon video
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Today's news is about a video game and a sad day in Korea. The company Activision makes the Call of Duty games. It has said sorry for using real news video in its newest game.

The game came out on October 23. Its story is about a war in Korea, but the war is made up. At the start of the game, there are about three seconds of real news video. It shows people trying to save a person on the ground after the Itaewon crowd crush.

That disaster happened in Seoul on October 29, 2022. A huge crowd filled a narrow street during Halloween, and 159 people died. The victims' families were shocked and asked the company to remove the scene.
According to news reports, the company sent its deepest sympathy and apologies to the families. It will delete the video in an update on November 12.
The story shows how strongly people still feel about the disaster. The apology came just after its fourth anniversary.
To sum up, the maker of Call of Duty said sorry and will remove the Itaewon video. Thank you for listening.

그 참사는 2022년 10월 29일 서울에서 일어났습니다. 핼러윈 때 엄청난 인파가 좁은 골목을 가득 메웠고, 159명이 숨졌습니다. 희생자 가족들은 충격을 받았고, 회사에 그 장면을 삭제해 달라고 요구했습니다.
보도에 따르면 회사는 가족들에게 깊은 위로와 사과의 뜻을 전했습니다. 회사는 11월 12일 업데이트에서 그 영상을 삭제할 예정입니다.
이번 일은 사람들이 아직도 그 참사에 대해 얼마나 깊이 느끼고 있는지를 보여 줍니다. 사과는 참사 4주기 직후에 나왔습니다.
요약하면, '콜 오브 듀티' 제작사가 사과했고 이태원 영상을 삭제할 예정입니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Call of Duty publisher apologizes for using Itaewon footage
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Our story today is about a video game and a real tragedy in Seoul. Activision, the company that publishes the Call of Duty games, has apologized for using real news footage in its newest game. Footage means recorded video. The company says it will remove the scenes.

The game, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, came out on October 23. Its story is about a fictional war on the Korean Peninsula. Fictional means it is made up and did not really happen. In the opening video, players noticed about three seconds of real news film. It showed people giving CPR to a person on the ground after the Itaewon crowd crush. CPR is emergency help to restart someone's heart and breathing.

The Itaewon crowd crush happened on October 29, 2022. During Halloween, a huge crowd filled a narrow street in Seoul, and 159 people died. Families of the victims and civic groups were shocked. They said the scene must be taken out of the game.

According to The Korea Herald, Activision sent its deepest condolences and apologies to the families. Condolences are words of sympathy for people who lost someone. The company said it did not mean to remind people of the disaster. It plans to delete the footage in an update on November 12.
Why does this matter? The apology came during the week of the disaster's fourth anniversary. The case also raises a question about how games and films should use real tragedies.
To sum up, the maker of Call of Duty has said sorry for using Itaewon disaster footage and will remove it from the game. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
오늘의 이야기는 비디오 게임과 서울에서 일어난 실제 비극에 관한 것입니다. '콜 오브 듀티' 게임을 배급하는 회사 액티비전이 최신 게임에 실제 뉴스 영상을 쓴 것에 대해 사과했습니다. 영상(footage)이란 녹화된 화면을 뜻합니다. 회사는 해당 장면들을 삭제하겠다고 밝혔습니다.

'콜 오브 듀티: 모던 워페어 4'라는 이 게임은 10월 23일에 나왔습니다. 게임 속 이야기는 한반도에서 벌어지는 허구의 전쟁입니다. 허구라는 것은 지어낸 것이고 실제로 일어나지 않았다는 뜻입니다. 플레이어들은 오프닝 영상에서 약 3초 분량의 실제 뉴스 화면을 발견했습니다. 이태원 압사 참사 직후 사람들이 바닥에 쓰러진 사람에게 심폐소생술을 하는 장면이었습니다. 심폐소생술(CPR)은 누군가의 심장과 호흡을 다시 살리기 위한 응급 처치입니다.
이태원 압사 참사는 2022년 10월 29일에 일어났습니다. 핼러윈 기간에 엄청난 인파가 서울의 좁은 골목을 가득 메웠고, 159명이 숨졌습니다. 희생자 가족들과 시민단체들은 충격을 받았습니다. 그들은 그 장면을 게임에서 반드시 빼야 한다고 말했습니다.
코리아헤럴드에 따르면 액티비전은 유가족들에게 깊은 애도와 사과의 뜻을 전했습니다. 애도란 누군가를 잃은 사람들에게 건네는 위로의 말입니다. 회사는 참사를 떠올리게 할 의도는 없었다고 말했습니다. 회사는 11월 12일 업데이트에서 그 영상을 삭제할 계획입니다.

요약하면, '콜 오브 듀티' 제작사가 이태원 참사 영상을 쓴 것에 대해 사과했고, 게임에서 그 영상을 삭제할 예정입니다. 들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Activision apologizes, will cut Itaewon footage from Call of Duty
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
The American video game publisher Activision has apologized for including real news footage of the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush in its latest Call of Duty title, and says the scenes will be removed.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which was released worldwide on October 23, is set during a fictional full-scale war on the Korean Peninsula. Its plot, which imagines a North Korean invasion of the South, had already sparked debate in Korea. Shortly after its launch, players noticed that the game's opening cinematic contained roughly three seconds of broadcast footage showing people performing CPR on a victim in the aftermath of the Itaewon disaster. The clip was apparently used to depict civilian casualties of the fictional conflict.

The crowd crush occurred on October 29, 2022, when Halloween crowds packed a narrow alley in Seoul's Itaewon district. A total of 159 people were killed. A group representing bereaved families, together with civic organizations, condemned the use of the footage and demanded its removal. A consumer group for gamers also called for an explanation and an apology.

Activision initially said the footage had been included to convey the game's fictional story and was not meant to reference any real tragedy. According to The Korea Herald, citing a report by the broadcaster MBC, the company then offered its deepest condolences and sincere apologies to the bereaved families. It said the footage will be deleted entirely in a game update scheduled for November 12.
The controversy came during the week of the disaster's fourth anniversary, a reminder that the tragedy remains a deeply sensitive issue in South Korea.
To sum up, Activision has apologized for using Itaewon disaster footage in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and plans to remove it in an update later this month. Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

이번 논란은 참사 4주기 주간에 일어났으며, 이 비극이 한국에서 여전히 매우 민감한 문제라는 점을 다시 보여 줍니다.

5.headline: Activision says sorry over Itaewon footage in new Call of Duty
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Activision, the publisher behind the blockbuster Call of Duty franchise, has issued a formal apology after it emerged that its latest release incorporated genuine news footage of the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush, one of the deadliest peacetime disasters in South Korea's recent history.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which hit shelves worldwide on October 23, is built around a fictional full-scale war on the Korean Peninsula. The premise, a North Korean invasion of the South, had already stirred debate at home even before the footage came to light. Within days of its launch, eagle-eyed players spotted roughly three seconds of broadcast footage in the game's opening cinematic depicting bystanders administering CPR to a victim in the immediate aftermath of the tragedy, apparently repurposed to illustrate civilian casualties in the game's invented conflict.

The disaster unfolded on the night of October 29, 2022, when Halloween revelers crammed into a narrow alley in Seoul's Itaewon district, claiming 159 lives. Unsurprisingly, the footage struck a raw nerve. An association of bereaved families, joined by civic groups, denounced its inclusion as senseless and demanded that it be taken out, while a gamers' consumer group called for a clear explanation and an apology.

Activision's first response, that the clip was merely meant to convey a fictional narrative, did little to quell the backlash. According to The Korea Herald, citing a report by the broadcaster MBC, the company has since extended its deepest condolences and sincere apologies to the bereaved families, stressing that it never intended to evoke the disaster or diminish the suffering it caused. The footage, it said, will be stripped out entirely in an update slated for November 12.

The timing could hardly have been more fraught, coming in the very week the nation marked the fourth anniversary of the crush. The episode also highlights a broader question for the entertainment industry: how to pursue realism without trampling on real-world grief.

To sum up, Activision has apologized for using Itaewon disaster footage in its new Call of Duty game and pledged to remove it, after an outcry from victims' families during the anniversary week. Thank you for listening.
